info.sub_ename: GUIDED READING OF GLOBAL ECONOMIC ISSUES

description.sub_ename: GUIDED READING OF GLOBAL ECONOMIC ISSUES
description.describe_ch: 本課程將從經濟史出發，介紹東西方經濟發展典範的差異以及衝突的成因，藉以進入近代經濟成長典範的建立以及考驗。最後，課程中談永續與未來，並定位台灣經濟的過去現在與展望。
description.describe_eh: This course explores economic history, highlighting differences and conflicts in Eastern and Western economic paradigms. It examines modern growth paradigms, sustainability, and future prospects. Specifically, it analyzes Taiwan's economic past, present, and future in relation to global economic dynamics.

gradeRuleDescribe.tpa_score_new:
Cheating & Plagiarism
  • For those who violate this rule, the assessment will be "no points" or the course will be "no points".
  • During the paper-and-pencil test, you are not allowed to talk, spy on other people’s test papers, or deliberately facilitate neighbors to peep, or entrainment, plagiarism, or transmission of materials, etc. If it is discovered, the test score for the offender will be counted as zero; it is a repeat offender Those who are involved will be dealt with in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Feng Chia University Student Reward and Punishment Measures.
  • If there is a test substitute, both parties involved in the fraud will be dealt with in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Feng Chia University Student Reward and Punishment Regulations.
  • Submit original works, any form of plagiarism is strictly prohibited. Those who violate this rule will be "not scored" for the assignment or "not scored" for the course, which will result in a failure in the semester grade of the course.
gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol:
Classroom behavior should always be timely, professional, well-prepared, and polite. Students, instructors, and guest speakers should maintain mutual dignity and respect to facilitate effective learning.
1. Students should attend classes punctually. If you cannot arrive on time, please do not enroll in the course. Unless you are ill or have an emergency, you should be present in the classroom and seated before the class begins. If you need to leave early, please inform the instructor in advance.
2. All students should respect everyone in the classroom and conduct themselves in a reasonable, responsible, and polite manner at all times.
3. Avoid talking, reading, sleeping, or working on unrelated tasks during class, except when engaged in group discussions. Minimize side conversations.
4. Laptops, tablets, and other devices may be used for note-taking, but should be put away otherwise.
5. Turn off and put away mobile phones, PDAs, and other devices, keeping them silent during class.
6. Wearing headphones during class is not permitted.
gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol_en:
Requirement: If you have never taken classes related to "economic quantitative analysis," please do not select this course.

All students are expected to adhere to the following communication guidelines:
1. Teaching and learning communication between teachers and students should utilize the o365 email as the common tool.
2. When communicating via email, announcements, or other means with teachers and classmates, ensure information is clear and maintain politeness.
3. Emails should be signed; anonymous emails will not receive a response.
4. For inquiries regarding course-related questions, please email during weekdays from Monday to Friday.
